Supermarket twin — realism pass v1

2026-09-14 · generated store look · branch fm/twin-realism-v1

Goal: the nine camera stills and the walkthrough should read as a real supermarket at a glance, so the twin is both a believable render set and a plausible visual domain for the shelf robot's perception. Every change lands in the generator (materials, lighting, placement), never a hand-edited .blend, so a headless rebuild reproduces it.

Render path: CPU Cycles, 64 samples, 1280×720, OpenImageDenoise. The RTX 3060 (12 GB) was held by the live ur10-cumotion Isaac/ROS stack (~5.8 GB; pgrep -af isaac non-empty), so per the task GPU rules the evidence renders fell back to CPU. No process was touched. Before and after use identical engine, samples and resolution.

1 · Gap audit

Three representative cameras rendered from the current main at evidence quality, gaps ranked by visual impact with a crop each.

1Flat, matte floor — no reflections, no wear

The floor is a dry, residential-looking terracotta tile with zero specular response. A real supermarket floor is buffed vinyl/porcelain that softly mirrors the ceiling LEDs and the products, with scuffed traffic lanes. This flatness is the single strongest 'this is CG' cue in every aisle shot.

2Cloned products — one SKU stamped N times

Every facing of a SKU is an identical copy at an identical angle and tone, so a shelf reads as one object repeated rather than many real packs. Real shelves have the same SKU too, but with print/lighting spread and hand-placed angles.

3Uniform plastic produce

The fruit is a grid of identical spheres — one size, one colour, one gloss — which reads as moulded plastic. Graded produce varies in size and shade.

4Clipped-flat lighting

The LED panels clip to flat white with no bloom, so highlights look computed rather than photographed; nothing on the floor picks the lights back up.

3 · What changed, per commit

Floor: polished commercial vinyl (reflections + traffic wear)
Rebuilds the imported Poly Haven tile material: a low-roughness clear coat for soft streaky reflections of the LEDs, a tightened base roughness so they read, and a large-scale procedural traffic-wear / grime layer so the floor is scuffed and non-uniform. Fixes gap 1.
Products & produce: per-instance variation to kill the cloned look
A per-instance brightness/saturation wobble (Object Info > Random, brand hue preserved) on every branded label, the fruit and the bread; wider yaw jitter, an occasional lean and per-facing depth jitter; and per-instance size grading for produce. Fixes gaps 2 and 3.
Lighting: photographic fog-glow bloom + exposure trim
A compositor fog-glow glare so the LED fixtures bloom softly instead of clipping flat, and exposure -0.3 -> -0.35 for highlight headroom now that the floor reflects the lights. Fixes gap 4.
Make the generator path-portable + add a CPU render path (enabler)
ROOT derives from each script's location so a rebuild is self-contained in any checkout; render_shots.py gains --cpu (CPU Cycles + OpenImageDenoise) for evidence renders while the GPU is held by the live robot stack.

After is marginally slower: the added clear-coat, per-instance variation and compositor fog-glow cost a little at the same sample count. Geometry is essentially unchanged (26,006 → 25,963 objects; the small delta is the new RNG draws reshuffling the empty/missing-facing pattern).

4 · USD export & pre-flight

Re-exported the realism-pass scene to USD (export_usd.py, 26 s) and ran the offline pre-flight scripts/preflight.py (no GPU): STORE PASS · ROBOT PASS · COMPOSER PASS → VERDICT PASS (exit 0). The new floor/label realism is procedural (clear coat, noise grime, per-instance Object-Info variation), which UsdPreviewSurface does not serialize, so the export carries the same base textures as before and introduces no new dangling references. The 6 floor/wall Poly Haven maps remain the documented COSMETIC standing defect (decision log 2026-09-10), auto-repaired by the pre-flight from assets/textures/.
